title: The method simulating spontaneous pain in patients with nociplastic pain using rats with fibromyalgia-like condition
author: Tanei, Miwa, et al.
materials: Nociplastic pain can occur without organic causes (e.g., inflammation or nerve damage) and is associated with various clinical disorders, including fibromyalgia [3]. It is emerging as a serious healthcare issue affecting those who have the disorder as well as social welfare [4]. Accordingly, preclinical research should contribute to the development of better therapies, where animal models are used for assessing the efficacy of therapeutic compounds under development. Because pain occurs in patients without an external stimulus, it is essential to assess spontaneous pain in animals [5]. The grimace scale was developed as a methodology for rating facial expression [6] and has been widely cited as a method for measuring spontaneous pain in animals [7], [8], [9]. However, the grimace scale score change in animals has been short-lived; thus, it is only useful in assessing pain in the early phase [8]. Furthermore, the grimace scale has never been applied to animals exhibiting nociplastic pain. Here, we applied the RGS reported by Sotocinal et al. [2]. to the reserpine-induced fibromyalgia-like rat, which manifests nociplastic pain caused by chronic depletion of endogenous monoamines [1] and demonstrated that a substantial and long-lasting elevation of RGS scores occurred in such rats. The measurement of RGS score in the reserpine-induced fibromyalgia-like rat simulates spontaneous pain in patients with nociplastic pain and may be related to the translation of efficacies of therapeutic compounds between animals and humans.

steps.title: House and allocate rats
steps.instruction: Acclimate male Sprague–Dawley rats (200–250 g) purchased from Clea Japan, Inc. Individually house them in acrylic cages with woodchip bedding, a 12 h light/dark cycle, temperature 23 ± 2 °C, humidity 55 ± 10 %, and provide standard chow and water ad libitum. Perform all tests during the light phase (08:00–20:00 h). Randomly allocate animals to experimental groups ensuring comparable body weight.

steps.title: Prepare reserpine injection solution
steps.instruction: Weigh reserpine (Nacalai Tesque, Kyoto, Japan) and transfer to a 1.5 mL microtube. Dissolve in glacial acetic acid (FUJIFILM Wako Pure Chemical Co., Osaka, Japan) with sonication. Dilute with distilled water to obtain a final concentration of 1 mg/mL reserpine in 0.5 % acetic acid.

steps.title: Inject reserpine or vehicle
steps.instruction: When each rat’s body weight is <300 g, inject the reserpine solution subcutaneously on the back at a volume of 1 mL/kg (equivalent to 1 mg/kg). Administer once daily for 3 consecutive days. Inject control animals with vehicle (0.5 % acetic acid, 1 mL/kg) on the same schedule.

steps.title: Videotape rats at scheduled time points
steps.instruction: Place each rat in an acrylic chamber (210 mm W × 105 mm D × 90 mm H) with a wire‑mesh ceiling. Record video for 30 min using two 1920 × 1080 px Jvc Gz‑E242‑S color cameras positioned in front and behind the chamber. Perform recordings at baseline (prior to injection) and on days 3, 5, 7, and 17 after the first injection.

steps.title: Capture still facial images
steps.instruction: Using Windows Media Player, play each 30‑min video and, at approximately 3‑min intervals when the rat’s head is motionless, capture a still image with the Print Screen function (Microsoft). Crop and enlarge the face to include eyes, nose/cheeks, ears, and whiskers. Obtain 10 facial images per animal.

steps.title: Prepare image set for scoring
steps.instruction: Insert the 10 images for each rat into PowerPoint 2013, one image per slide. Randomize slide order. Ensure each image is clear and in‑focus for the four facial regions.

steps.title: Train raters with reference images
steps.instruction: Create a training set consisting of 15 representative images from control (vehicle) rats and 15 from reserpine‑treated rats (selected from days 3, 5, 7 recordings). Provide the set as a PowerPoint file (File 1) and present images in random order to three blinded raters for practice.

steps.title: Score images and compute RGS
steps.instruction: For each image, have three trained raters independently score four action units—orbital tightening, nose/cheek flattening, ear changes, whisker changes—using a 3‑point Likert scale (0 = absent, 1 = moderate, 2 = obvious) as described by Sotocinal et al. Compute the average of the four units for each image, then average the three raters’ scores to obtain the rat grimace scale (RGS) for that image. Finally, calculate each animal’s overall RGS as the mean of its 10 image scores.
